title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
gist: Recent studies show warming-driven emissions from permafrost, wildfires, lakes and wetlands could add 0.2-0.4°C on top of the expected 2.6°C by 2100 and shorten the time to breaching 1.5°C/2°C by up to 25%, yet UN-report models largely omit these feedbacks. A 20+ team model intercomparison aims to feed the 2029 UN assessment, while early-stage interventions (fire suppression, wetland chemistry, permafrost mats) remain unproven at scale.

insights.claim: A September study in Environmental Research Letters found extra CO2 and methane from thawing permafrost, intensifying wildfires, hotter lakes and reservoirs, and warmer wetter wetlands could add 0.2°C to 0.4°C of global warming this century.
insights.speaker: James Temple
insights.so_what: Warming tails are fatter than consensus projections; physical climate risk is underpriced.
insights.quote: could drive global average temperatures up 0.2 °C to 0.4 °C this century
insights.locator: A study in Environmental Research Letters

insights.claim: The feedback-driven warming would come on top of the roughly 2.6°C above preindustrial levels that modelers already expect through 2100.
